content: 游客开始“住久一点”，酒店为什么还只会做一晚生意？
暑期旅游媒体正在讨论一种值得酒店关注的旅行方式：从“打卡”转向“住久一点”。封面新闻在7月底以“从特种兵到慢充”概括这种消费变化，华龙网援引去哪儿信息称暑期酒店预订处于高位。对酒店而言，真正值得追问的不是所有客人是否都住得更久，而是当客人选择连续停留时，酒店能不能把多出的每一天接好。
入住天数增加，客人的满意度未必同步上升。如果第二晚、第三晚的体验和第一晚几乎没有区别，即使客人没有当场投诉，也可能得出一个结论：“也就这样了。”
很多酒店把“客人连住”理解成了“少做两次入住手续”。只要客人不换房，第二天的服务和第一天几乎没有区别：同一个时间段敲门打扫、同一份早餐、同一套欢迎语。执行标准看起来没有问题，但客人已经开始觉得无聊了。
五个被忽视的经营断点
第一，预订阶段没有帮助客人理解“这里适合住几天”。大多数酒店的预订页面和确认消息只会确认入住日期和退房日期，不会告诉客人每天可以做什么、哪些体验需要提前预约。客人带着“到了再说”的心态入住，酒店也就失去了提前安排服务的窗口。
第二，入住时的介绍只有房间，没有节奏。一个要住三晚的客人不仅需要早餐时间、Wi-Fi密码和退房时间，还需要知道周边哪些地方适合第一天探索、哪家餐厅需要提前预订、雨天有什么备用计划。
第三，客房服务仍按“一晚客”设计。第一晚之后，客人可能不需要全套布草更换，却可能更需要补充饮用水、调整空调设置或增加晾衣架。如果客房部每天同一时间敲门、按照同一套标准执行，客人会觉得酒店没有注意到自己已经住了一段时间。
第四，餐饮和公共空间的体验缺少变化。连续几天吃同样的早餐，再好的出品也会让人疲劳。大堂吧、健身房和公共休息区同样需要说明什么时候适合安静使用、什么时候适合社交，而不是让客人完全靠猜。
第五，离店前没有承接。连住了几天的客人对酒店和周边已经建立熟悉感。离店前如果能结合其实际停留给出下一次建议，客人感受到的是被记住，而不只是统一的“欢迎再次光临”。
一个判断框架：酒店真的具备连续停留的能力吗？
停留理由：客人预订时是否已经知道在这里可以做什么、适合住几天？
每日变化：第二晚、第三晚的体验和第一晚是否不同？
服务节奏：客房、餐饮和公共空间是否根据入住天数调整节奏？
增量消费：连住期间是否有自然增购的路径，例如餐饮、洗衣、在地体验或房型升级？
复购线索：离店时酒店是否掌握了客人下次可能再来的原因？
这五个问题不需要一次性全部解决。但如果一家酒店连一个都回答不上来，那么“住得更久”目前还只是多收了几天房费，没有变成真正的经营优势。房晚变长不等于价值自然增长。客人多住的每一天，酒店都在用服务回答：是让客人觉得“选对了”，还是让客人觉得“住够了”。
常见问题
酒店怎样提高客人的平均停留时间？
关键不只在价格优惠，更在停留理由。酒店需要在预订阶段讲清楚目的地能提供几天的内容，并让每天的服务有节奏变化。
连住客人最在意哪些服务？
酒店可以从客房清洁的灵活度、早餐是否有变化、周边信息是否实用三个检查点入手，再回看本店连住客的评价和反馈，确认问题集中在哪些环节。
酒店如何设计适合住两三晚的产品？
可以围绕城市慢旅行、家庭度假或在地体验，把住宿、早餐变化、周边路线建议和退房安排组成连贯产品，而不是一组互不关联的服务项目。
连住优惠为什么不一定带来更多利润？
只在价格上让步，并不会自动创造餐饮、洗衣、在地体验或房型升级等增量价值。酒店仍需要结合自身成本和客人需求核算产品。
对于正在重新审视连续停留能力的酒店，从客人入住动线出发做一次系统经营诊断，可以帮助定位服务和收益结构中的断点。了解更多：marvelbros.com/zh/hotel-operation-improvement
contentEn: Travelers Are Staying Longer. Why Are Hotels Still Built for One-Night Stays?

Summer travel coverage in China is drawing attention to a shift from checklist tourism toward slower trips and longer stays in one place. For hotels, the useful question is not whether every guest now stays longer. It is whether the operation can deliver more value when a guest chooses a multi-night stay.

Chinese travel media reported in late July that some travelers are moving from rushing between landmarks to settling in and staying put. At the same time, booking-platform reporting indicates that summer hotel demand remains high. Neither signal guarantees longer stays for every hotel, but together they make multi-night service capability a timely operating question.
Most hotels still treat a three-night stay as three copies of a one-night stay: the same cleaning schedule, breakfast spread and welcome script. Nothing changes, and guests notice.
Five Overlooked Operational Breakpoints

First, the booking stage never helps guests answer a basic question: how long is this place worth staying in? Most booking pages confirm dates but do not explain what guests can do each day or which experiences need advance reservations.

Second, check-in orientation covers the room but not the rhythm. A three-night guest needs more than breakfast hours, Wi-Fi and checkout time. They need useful day-one ideas, reservation advice and a rainy-day alternative.

Third, housekeeping is still designed around one-night guests. After the first night, a guest may not need a full linen change but may want water replenished, a different cleaning time or an extra drying rack.

Fourth, dining and public spaces lack variation. The same breakfast several mornings running can feel repetitive. Hotels should also help guests understand when shared spaces are best for quiet use and when they are more social.
Fifth, there is no follow-up before departure. After several days, the hotel knows more about the guest. A relevant next-stay suggestion can make the guest feel remembered rather than processed.
A Judgment Framework for Multi-Night Capability
Reason for staying: Did guests know what they could do here and how many days might suit the trip when booking?
Daily variation: Is night two or three meaningfully different from night one?
Service rhythm: Have housekeeping, dining and public-space operations adjusted to length of stay?
Incremental spending: Is there a natural path to dining, laundry, local experiences or room upgrades?
Return signals: At checkout, does the hotel understand why the guest might choose it again?
Longer room nights do not mean value grows automatically. Every additional day gives the hotel another chance to confirm that the guest chose well, or to make the stay feel repetitive.
Frequently Asked Questions
How can hotels encourage guests to stay longer?
Start with reasons to stay, not only discounts. Explain what the destination offers across several days and design a service rhythm that changes with the stay.
What should hotels check for multi-night guests?
Review cleaning flexibility, breakfast variation and the usefulness of local information, then compare those questions with feedback from the hotel's own multi-night guests.
How do hotels design a two- or three-night package?
Build one coherent experience around a real trip purpose, combining accommodation, daily variation, local guidance and departure arrangements rather than listing unrelated add-ons.
Why do multi-night discounts not always improve profit?
A lower rate does not automatically create additional value. Hotels still need to assess costs, guest fit and credible paths to dining, laundry, local experiences or upgrades.
Hotels reviewing their multi-night capability can begin with an operational diagnosis of the complete guest journey. Learn more: marvelbros.com/en/hotel-operation-improvement
